find: -cf - LICENSE NOTICE contracts | gzip -n
why: The release archive must contain the complete project license.

find: python3 "${verifier}" "${temporary}" \
why: An archive missing a declared text must not replace a valid prior artifact.

find: if license_id not in COMMUNITY:
why: A license outside the policy must be refused by name, not judged as a community license.

find: if not obligations:
why: A Llama or Gemma model without recorded obligations would ship without the notices its license demands.

find: bad += license_problems(d.name, spec)
why: check.sh reaches the license rule only through the metadata check; dropping the call passes any license.

find: if case["expected_ids"] is None:
why: A contract case without recorded tokens must fail and print them, never pass on the text check alone.

find: if case["must_contain"] not in text:
why: The recorded tokens could encode a wrong answer; the decoded text must still name the expected fact.

find: if not cases:
why: A model directory no case names would publish with no decode checked at all.

find: info.mtime = 0
why: Releases are immutable and hashed; an archive that changes with file times cannot be rebuilt to the same bytes.

find: (doc / "copyright").write_text("\n".join(p.read_text() for p in notices))
why: The model package must carry the license and notice that the model's license obliges every redistribution to ship.

find: if not _number(entry["score"]) or entry["score"] < threshold:
why: Rule 1: an expected detection under the threshold, or with a score that is no number, would teach three decoders to keep it.

find: if not _count(entry["class"]) or not class_range[0] <= entry["class"] <= class_range[1]:
why: Rule 2: an expected class 80 or -1 has no name in any detector and must not reach a consumer as the reference.

find: if not _number(row[5]) or math.trunc(row[5]) != entry["class"]:
why: Rule 2: the class id is the row's number cut to an integer; a rounded 15.9 would be recorded as class 16.

find: if not all(map(_number, row[:4])) or row[2] < row[0] or row[3] < row[1]:
why: Rule 3: a row with a NaN corner or with x2 before x1 is no detection, so no expected detection may name it.

find: if box[2] < box[0] or box[3] < box[1]:
why: Rule 3: an expected box whose corners are out of order cannot come from a kept row.

find: if len(kept) != len(case["rows"]):
why: Rule 4: a suppression case that drops a row would pass the detector that merged the two cats.

find: if not any(_iou(a["box"], b["box"]) > SUPPRESSION_IOU for a, b in pairs):
why: Rule 4: without a same-class pair above IoU 0.45 the case passes a detector that still suppresses at 0.45.

find: if min(box) < 0 or max(box[0], box[2]) > case["width"] or max(box[1], box[3]) > case["height"]:
why: Rule 5: an expected box past the frame edge would undo the cut the owner decided for all three detectors.

find: if row <= last:
why: Consumers compare the lists in order; an expected list out of row order fails every decoder that is right.

find: if entry["score"] != row[4]:
why: A mistyped expected score fails every consumer; it must fail here first.

find:
if not isinstance(box, list) or len(box) != 4 or not all(_number(v) and v == math.trunc(v) for v in box):
        return ["the box is not four whole pixel numbers"]
replace:
if not isinstance(box, list) or len(box) != 4 or not all(_number(v) for v in box):
        return ["the box is not four whole pixel numbers"]
why: OrchestrANT cuts coordinates to integers; a fractional expected box could only be met by the float decoders.

find: elif not all(_number(value) or value in NON_FINITE for value in row):
why: A row value outside the three spellings is read differently, or not at all, by the three languages' parsers.

find: return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), parse_constant=refuse)
why: Python accepts a bare NaN; serde_json and nlohmann do not, so the Rust and C++ tests could not open the file.

find: if not all(math.isclose(scale * side, size) for scale, side, size in zip(scales, frame, content)):
why: A mapping that no preprocessing returns makes the expected boxes fit no frame.

find: bad += [f"rule {rule} has no decode case" for rule in RULES if all(case["rule"] != rule for case in cases)]
why: A rule without a case holds no detector to it.

find: bad = [f"{label} {name} is missing: a published case stays" for name in published if name not in found]
why: A deleted case silently removes a rule from three consumers' tests at their next pin.

find: elif digest != published[name]:
why: A published case changes only with schema_version (AGENTS.md); an edited row must not pass as the same case.

find: if name not in published:
why: Recording a new case's digest is the reviewed step that makes it a published case.

find: return 1 if bad else 0
why: check.sh stops on the status alone; printed problems with status 0 would pass CI.

find: for key in METADATA_KEYS if written.get(key) not in listed[key]]
why: A model.json naming a layout or preprocessing no consumer knows must fail before it is exported.

find: if LAYOUT not in listed["kataglyphis.output"]:
why: The decode cases are for one kataglyphis.output value; the list must still allow it.

find: if not isinstance(decode, dict) or set(decode) != DECODE_KEYS:
why: A contract without the decode section, or without its order or a tolerance, gives a consumer nothing to compare by.

find:
if not isinstance(cases, list) or not cases:
        return ["decode.cases must be a non-empty list"]
replace:
if False:
        return ["decode.cases must be a non-empty list"]
why: A decode section whose cases are gone must be named as that, not as five rules without a case.

find: if not isinstance(case, dict) or set(case) != CASE_KEYS:
why: A case that lacks a field, such as its mapping or its threshold, cannot be replayed by any consumer.

find:
if not isinstance(case["name"], str) or not case["name"]:
        return ["a decode case needs a name"]
replace:
if False:
        return ["a decode case needs a name"]
why: Consumers list the cases they replay by name; a nameless case can be neither listed nor reported.

find: if not _count(case["rule"]) or case["rule"] not in RULES:
why: A case filed under no rule escapes the check that every rule has a case.

find: if not _number(case["score_threshold"]) or not 0 < case["score_threshold"] <= 1:
why: A threshold of 0 keeps every finite score, so the case would show nothing about rule 1.

find: if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows:
why: A case without rows replays nothing and still counts as a case of its rule.

find: if not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != 6:
why: A row of five values has no class column; each consumer would read past its end in its own way.

find: if not isinstance(expected, list):
why: Consumers compare two lists entry by entry; anything else under expected fails them all at the first read.

find: if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != EXPECTED_KEYS:
why: An expected detection without its class, score or box leaves that part of a decoder's answer uncompared.

find: if not _count(row) or row >= len(rows):
why: Every rule check reads the row an expected detection names; a row that is none checks nothing.

find: if not all(_count(size) and size for size in sizes) or case["mode"] not in ("stretch", "letterbox"):
why: A mode other than stretch or letterbox names no preprocessing any consumer has.

find: if not isinstance(mapping, dict) or set(mapping) != MAPPING_KEYS:
why: A consumer fills its own mapping type from the six fields of the preprocessing cases; a seventh or a missing one breaks that.

find: if not all(map(_count, whole)) or 0 in whole[:2]:
why: A negative padding or an empty content area is no result of any preprocessing.

find: if not all(_number(mapping[key]) and mapping[key] > 0 for key in ("scale_x", "scale_y")):
why: Every decoder divides by the scale; a scale of zero must be named as that.

find: if any(pad + size > limit for pad, size, limit in zip(pads, content, room)):
why: Padding plus content wider than the input is no letterbox, and boxes mapped through it fit no frame.

find: if case["mode"] == "stretch" and (pads != (0, 0) or content != room):
why: A letterbox mapping under the name stretch would be fed to a consumer's stretch path.

find: if decode["layout"] != LAYOUT:
why: The rules and rows are for xyxy_score_class; under another name a consumer would hand them to a raw-head decoder.

find: if decode["non_finite"] != NON_FINITE:
why: The three spellings are the ones the float parsers of Rust, C++ and Python all read.

find: if decode["order"] != "row":
why: The expected lists are in row order; another stated order would fail every decoder that is right.

find: if not _number(section[key]) or not 0 < section[key] < limit:
why: A coordinate tolerance of a pixel, or a score tolerance of 0.01, would pass a decoder that is off by that much.

find: if not isinstance(rules, list) or [str(rule)[:3] for rule in rules] != [f"{rule}. " for rule in RULES]:
why: The contract states the five rules in words; a dropped rule leaves its cases unexplained.

find: bad += [f"case name {name} is used twice" for name in sorted(set(names)) if names.count(name) > 1]
why: Consumers pick cases by name; of two cases with one name a consumer replays one twice and the other never.

find: if not isinstance(listed, dict) or any(key not in listed for key in METADATA_KEYS):
why: A contract that stops listing one of the two keys leaves model.json's value for it unchecked.

find: for key, values in listed.items() if not _names(values)]
replace: for key, values in listed.items() if False]
why: An empty or repeated list of values is nothing a model.json can be checked against.

find: if dropped and not _suppressed_by_kept(index, kept, scored):
why: A raw case that drops a confident candidate no kept one suppresses would hand every detector a wrong set (hub CON288 (e)).

find: if candidates != sorted(candidates, key=lambda index: (-scored[index][1], index)):
why: Raw-head detections come in descending score, ties to the lower candidate; a case out of that order misleads every replay.

find: if not isinstance(digest, str) or len(digest) != 64 or set(digest) - set("0123456789abcdef"):
why: A digest case whose expected SHA-256 is no SHA-256 can never be matched by a detector's tensor.

find: SHA256 c6cd81c5125e0772096c6e2968353c758bb5ecb3b2dbf7ec2d1c522b57c75f0f
why: the detectors pin the PNG's bytes; a re-encode with another digest must fail here first
